description: Sou Giancarllo, engenheiro mecatrônico e professor na UniRV, doutorando em Eng. de Produção (UFPE). Apaixonado por IA aplicada ao agro, lidero a equipe MyRoça no desafio "Adaptando fazendas com dados da NASA": um Gêmeo Digital da Fazenda com previsões e recomendações ao produtor. J
summary: SpaceAgro is an open web application (Apache-2.0) that supports three farm decisions: what to plant, when to plant and how to rotate crops. It integrates NASA POWER weather series, Landsat 8/9 crop-health indicators (NDVI, NDMI) per field, ECOSTRESS evaporative stress, NASA GIBS imagery and FIRMS fire detections with the field map, climate-risk zoning (ZARC), CONAB yield series, Embrapa rotation rules, market prices and a crop diary. A season planner compares crop sequences by estimated margin and risk per hectare, and the assistant Estrela answers in plain language, by text or voice, citing the data source. The challenge addresses the gap between available Earth-observation data and farm decisions. Poorly timed planting reduced soybean yield by about 5% in Goiás in 2025/26 (R$ 420/ha); SpaceAgro makes timing and field-condition information accessible to producers with low digital literacy.
details:
SpaceAgro is an open web application (Apache-2.0) that supports planting, rotation and season decisions at field level. The farmer maps field boundaries on a satellite map; the platform attaches NASA data, official agronomic rules and market data to each field and returns recommendations in plain language. The demonstration farm uses the public CAR boundary of a 10,387 ha property in Rio Verde, Goiás (property limit, legal reserve, native vegetation, permanent-preservation areas, spring, airstrip and 20 fields).

HOW IT WORKS

1. Weather: NASA POWER daily series (rainfall, temperature, radiation, humidity) at each field centroid feed the planting-window assessment, the crop diary and a 30-day water balance. Evapotranspiration and soil moisture (ERA5-Land via Open-Meteo) and a 3-day rainfall forecast complete a low/medium/high water-risk level per field.

2. Crop health: Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 scenes (NASA/USGS, via Microsoft Planetary Computer) are processed by a scheduled routine into NDVI and NDMI per field. Each value is compared with the expected curve for the crop stage, with similar fields and with the weak-zone share of the field; deviations are flagged on the map.

3. Water stress: ECOSTRESS ECO_L4T_ESI (evaporative stress index, ~70 m, NASA) is retrieved daily through earthaccess (GitHub Actions); each field shows the exact image date, the rainfall measured since then (NASA POWER) and an attention level.

4. Map layers: HLS L30 (Landsat 8/9, 30 m) and GIBS layers (VIIRS, MODIS NDVI, GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP soil moisture, MODIS land-surface temperature). NASA FIRMS (VIIRS 375 m) fire detections generate alerts near the farm.

5. Season planner: climate-risk zoning (ZARC), CONAB series, Embrapa rotation rules and market prices (FRED commodity series, CBOT/ICE futures curves, exchange rate) compare crop sequences by margin per hectare in pessimistic, base and optimistic scenarios, with yield adjusted by strategy risk. The combined-decision banner selects the highest base margin among options without high risk; price and cost are editable and a -40% to +40% price test recomputes the decision.

6. Crop diary: records for tillage, liming, planting, fertilisation, pest and disease control, irrigation, measured rain, monitoring, harvest and weather events; daily weather is filled automatically from NASA POWER and Open-Meteo.

7. Yield forecast: the CONAB mean for Goiás is adjusted by the farmer's harvests (Bayesian update, 10-90% range); with four recorded harvests the mean absolute error for soybean falls from 5.9 to 4.3 sc/ha.

8. Statistical models (Colab, IBGE yields 2016-2025 for 28 municipalities in southwest Goiás × NASA POWER, MODIS, SoilGrids, SRTM; 7 model families, validated by year and by municipality): for a new farm without history, NASA and soil data reduce the error from 5.4 to 4.7 sc/ha in soybean and from 13.2 to 10.0 sc/ha in maize; for known municipalities the historical trend remained the best predictor (4.8 and 13.8 sc/ha).

Estrela, the assistant, answers by voice or text in plain, WhatsApp-style language using these data, cites the source of each figure and can register diary entries on request. Planting, rotation and risk recommendations come from explicit, auditable rules in the code (ZARC, Embrapa, climate thresholds), not from a generative model.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Earlier detection of stressed fields, planting decisions tied to rainfall and the climate window, and crop-sequence comparison with explicit margin and risk. The intended impact is to reduce yield and revenue losses from poorly timed planting (about 5% yield loss in Goiás in 2025/26, around R$ 420/ha) and to make Earth-observation data usable by producers with low digital literacy, at low cost.

TOOLS

TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL JS, IndexedDB; Python (Landsat/MODIS/ECOSTRESS processing, statistical models in Google Colab); Cloudflare Workers (assistant); GitHub Pages and GitHub Actions (scheduled data routines); PostgreSQL (accounts and farms); Claude (Anthropic) as the language model of Estrela and for development support; interface in six languages (Portuguese, Spanish, English, German, French, Mandarin).

CREATIVE ASPECT

A conversational agronomist grounded in satellite data: the farmer asks in everyday language and receives an answer tied to the specific field, the date of the satellite image and the cited source. An opening sequence takes the user from orbit to the farm; a digital twin shows each field with colour and texture by crop and phase.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Low digital literacy (simple mode, voice, short answers); cost (static site, free public data); transparency (source and image date shown, rules open to audit); local relevance (ZARC, CONAB, Embrapa, Brazilian equivalents of US datasets); data latency (image age is always displayed); language access; and demonstration on a real farm boundary.
dataRefs: NASA POWER – daily rainfall, temperature, radiation and humidity
NASA GIBS / Worldview – VIIRS, MODIS NDVI, GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP soil moisture, MODIS land-surface temperature layers
NASA FIRMS – VIIRS 375 m active fire detections
Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 (NASA/USGS) – NDVI and NDMI per field
Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 HLSL30 v2.0 – 30 m true-colour layer
ECOSTRESS ECO_L4T_ESI v002 – evaporative stress index, 70 m	https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/data/catalog/lpcloud-
MODIS MOD13Q1 v6.1 – NDVI/EVI time series
MODIS MCD15A2H v6.1 – LAI/FPAR time series
MODIS MOD16A2 v6.1 – evapotranspiration time series
NASA Earthdata – access (earthaccess) to ECOSTRESS, IMERG and SMAP
projectRefs: Microsoft Planetary Computer – Landsat and MODIS data mirror (COG)
Open-Meteo – weather forecast and recent history (CC BY 4.0)
ERA5-Land reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Data Store – evapotranspiration and soil moisture (via Open-Meteo)
FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis – commodity prices (IMF series)
Yahoo Finance – CBOT and ICE futures curves
ZARC – Agricultural Climate Risk Zoning (MAPA, Brazil)
CONAB – crop surveys and yield series (Brazil)
SICAR – Rural Environmental Registry (CAR) public boundaries
Esri World Imagery – default satellite basemap
Claude (Anthropic) – language model for Estrela and code assistance
